sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: All enrolled members are eligible for emergency room coverage. Coverage applies 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, including holidays. Members must present their insurance card at the time of service.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Emergency room copay is $350 per visit. Annual deductible of $1,500 applies before copay. After meeting the deductible, the plan pays 80% and the member pays 20% coinsurance. Out-of-pocket maximum is $6,000 per individual per year.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Preauthorization is NOT required for true emergency room visits. A true emergency is defined as a sudden, serious medical condition that requires immediate treatment to prevent death or serious harm.

sections.title: Out-of-Network
sections.content: Emergency room services are covered at in-network rates regardless of whether the facility is in-network, as required by the No Surprises Act. Balance billing protections apply.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Ambulance transport is covered when medically necessary and when transport by other means would endanger the member's health.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Ground ambulance: $250 copay per transport. Air ambulance: $500 copay per transport. Deductible of $1,500 applies. After deductible, plan covers 80%.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Preauthorization is not required for emergency ambulance transport. Non-emergency ambulance transport requires prior authorization from the plan.

sections.title: Exclusions
sections.content: Non-emergency transport for convenience, transport to a facility beyond the nearest appropriate facility, and air transport when ground transport is medically appropriate are not covered.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: All enrolled members may use in-network urgent care centers for conditions that require prompt attention but are not life-threatening emergencies.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: In-network urgent care copay is $75 per visit. Deductible does not apply to urgent care copay. Out-of-network urgent care is subject to deductible and 40% coinsurance.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: No preauthorization required for urgent care visits. Members should use urgent care rather than emergency rooms for non-emergency conditions to minimize costs.

sections.title: Scope of Services
sections.content: Urgent care covers minor fractures, lacerations, infections, flu, strep throat, minor burns, and similar conditions. Chest pain, stroke symptoms, and severe difficulty breathing require emergency room care.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.content: Observation status is an outpatient service where a patient is monitored while a physician determines whether inpatient admission is warranted. Inpatient admission requires a physician order and medical necessity determination.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Observation stays are billed as outpatient services: $350 ER copay plus applicable outpatient facility fees. Inpatient admission: $500 per-admission copay, then plan pays 90% after deductible.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Inpatient admission from the emergency room requires notification within 24 hours of admission. Observation stays do not require preauthorization.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Elective surgeries are covered when medically necessary and performed by an in-network surgeon at an in-network facility. Member must be continuously enrolled for 90 days prior to the procedure.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Inpatient surgical facility fee: $500 per admission copay. Surgeon fee: plan pays 80% after deductible. Anesthesia: plan pays 80% after deductible. Annual deductible $1,500 applies.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: All elective surgeries require preauthorization at least 5 business days before the scheduled procedure. Failure to obtain preauthorization may result in denial of coverage.

sections.title: Second Opinion
sections.content: Members are encouraged to seek a second surgical opinion at no additional cost. Plan covers second opinion consultations at the specialist copay rate of $50.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Emergency surgery is covered when immediate surgical intervention is necessary to prevent death, serious disability, or significant deterioration of health.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Emergency surgery copay is $500 per admission. Plan pays 80% of covered services after deductible. No separate surgeon or anesthesia copay for emergency procedures.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Preauthorization is NOT required for emergency surgical procedures. Plan must be notified within 48 hours of emergency surgery or as soon as reasonably possible.

sections.title: Post-Surgical Care
sections.content: Follow-up visits within 90 days of surgery are covered at the primary care copay rate of $25. Physical therapy ordered by the surgeon is covered under the physical therapy benefit.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Bariatric surgery is covered for members with BMI >= 40, or BMI >= 35 with one or more obesity-related comorbidities (Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, sleep apnea). Member must have documented failure of supervised weight loss program for minimum 6 months.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Bariatric surgery: $500 inpatient copay plus 20% coinsurance after deductible. Nutritional counseling: covered at preventive care rate. Pre-surgical psychological evaluation: $50 specialist copay.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Preauthorization is required. Submission must include BMI documentation, comorbidity records, 6-month weight loss program records, nutritional assessment, and psychological evaluation.

sections.title: Exclusions
sections.content: Purely cosmetic surgical procedures resulting from weight loss (e.g., panniculectomy) are not covered unless medically necessary. Revision surgeries require separate preauthorization.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Outpatient surgery is covered when the procedure can be safely performed without overnight hospitalization and is medically necessary.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Outpatient ambulatory surgery center: $200 facility copay. Hospital outpatient department: $250 facility copay. Surgeon fee covered at 80% after deductible. No separate anesthesia copay.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Outpatient surgeries require preauthorization 3 business days in advance. Preauthorization may be waived for minor procedures under $500 total cost.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: All enrolled members are eligible for outpatient mental health services. Coverage is parity-compliant under the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA).

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Individual therapy: $25 copay per session (same as primary care). Group therapy: $15 copay per session. Psychological testing: $50 copay. No visit limits apply.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: First 8 outpatient therapy sessions per calendar year do not require preauthorization. Sessions 9 and beyond require preauthorization demonstrating ongoing medical necessity.

sections.title: Providers
sections.content: Covered providers include licensed psychologists, licensed clinical social workers (LCSW), licensed professional counselors (LPC), licensed marriage and family therapists (LMFT), and psychiatrists.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Inpatient psychiatric care is covered when the member presents a danger to self or others, or when intensive monitoring and stabilization is required that cannot be achieved in outpatient settings.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Inpatient psychiatric: $500 per admission copay, then plan pays 80% after deductible. Partial hospitalization program (PHP): $75 per day copay. Intensive outpatient program (IOP): $25 per day copay.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Preauthorization required for planned inpatient psychiatric admission. Emergency involuntary holds (5150) do not require preauthorization; plan must be notified within 24 hours.

sections.title: Length of Stay
sections.content: Initial authorization for 7 days. Continued stay reviews every 7 days thereafter. Discharge planning begins on day 3 of admission. Step-down to PHP or IOP required when clinically appropriate.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Substance use disorder (SUD) treatment is covered at parity with medical benefits per MHPAEA. Coverage includes alcohol, opioid, and other substance use disorders.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Outpatient SUD counseling: $25 copay per session. Intensive outpatient SUD: $25 per day. Residential SUD treatment: $500 per admission, then 80% after deductible. Medication-assisted treatment (MAT): covered under pharmacy benefit.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Residential SUD treatment requires preauthorization. Outpatient SUD counseling does not require preauthorization for first 12 sessions. MAT medications require step therapy: buprenorphine preferred over methadone unless clinically justified.

sections.title: Coverage Limits
sections.content: No annual or lifetime limits on SUD treatment benefits. Residential treatment covered up to 30 days per episode of care; additional days require continued stay review.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Telehealth mental health services are covered for all enrolled members. Video visits are covered equivalent to in-person visits. Audio-only telehealth is covered when video is not available to the member.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Telehealth mental health: $25 copay per session (same as in-person). No additional facility fee for telehealth. Deductible does not apply to telehealth mental health visits.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: No preauthorization required for telehealth mental health sessions 1-8 per year. Same preauthorization rules apply for sessions 9+ as in-person care.

sections.title: Formulary Tiers
sections.content: Tier 1 (Generic): $10 copay per 30-day supply. Tier 2 (Preferred Brand): $40 copay per 30-day supply. Tier 3 (Non-Preferred Brand): $80 copay per 30-day supply. Tier 4 (Specialty): 20% coinsurance, max $200 per fill.

sections.title: Mail Order
sections.content: Mail order pharmacy provides 90-day supply for cost of 2 copays (Tier 1: $20, Tier 2: $80, Tier 3: $160). Mail order required for maintenance medications after 2 retail fills.

sections.title: Step Therapy
sections.content: Non-preferred brand drugs require step therapy: member must try and fail a Tier 1 or Tier 2 drug before Tier 3 is covered. Step therapy exceptions available with physician documentation of medical necessity.

sections.title: Specialty Drugs
sections.content: Specialty drugs must be dispensed through designated specialty pharmacy. Prior authorization required for all specialty drugs. Copay assistance programs apply automatically when available.

sections.title: PA Requirements
sections.content: Prior authorization (PA) is required for specialty drugs, certain brand-name drugs, drugs used off-label, drugs with high abuse potential, and drugs requiring clinical monitoring.

sections.title: Approval Process
sections.content: PA requests reviewed within 72 hours for standard requests. Urgent PA requests reviewed within 24 hours. Emergency supply of 72-hour supply may be dispensed at retail pharmacy pending PA determination.

sections.title: Appeals
sections.content: PA denials may be appealed within 180 days. First-level appeal reviewed within 30 days (7 days for urgent). Expedited appeal available when member's health is at risk.

sections.title: Auto-renewal
sections.content: Approved PAs are valid for 12 months unless otherwise specified. PA auto-renewal submitted 60 days before expiration for ongoing treatments.

sections.title: Initial Prescriptions
sections.content: Initial opioid prescriptions for acute pain limited to 7-day supply. Initial prescriptions for chronic pain or cancer pain: 30-day supply covered without PA.

sections.title: Quantity Limits
sections.content: Opioid quantity limits align with CDC guidelines: 50 morphine milligram equivalents (MME) per day without PA. Doses above 90 MME per day require PA with documentation of failure of lower-dose regimen.

sections.title: Monitoring Requirements
sections.content: Members receiving long-term opioid therapy (>90 days) must have urine drug screen every 6 months and pain management agreement on file. Non-compliance may result in coverage suspension.

sections.title: Naloxone Co-Prescribing
sections.content: Naloxone co-prescription covered at $0 copay for members receiving opioid prescriptions exceeding 50 MME per day or when risk factors for overdose are present.

sections.title: Insulin Copay Cap
sections.content: Insulin copay capped at $35 per 30-day supply regardless of formulary tier. Cap applies to all insulin types: rapid-acting, long-acting, and combination insulins. Deductible does not apply to insulin.

sections.title: Coverage
sections.content: All FDA-approved insulins covered on formulary. Preferred insulins (Tier 1): insulin glargine (generic), NPH insulin. Non-preferred insulins available without step therapy for members with documented history.

sections.title: Supplies
sections.content: Diabetes supplies (syringes, pen needles, lancets, test strips) covered under durable medical equipment benefit. Continuous glucose monitors (CGM) covered at $50 copay for eligible diabetic members.

sections.title: Coverage
sections.content: Preventive care services recommended by the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) with an A or B rating are covered at $0 cost-sharing when performed by an in-network provider.

sections.title: Annual Wellness Visit
sections.content: Annual wellness visit: $0 copay for adults 18+. Includes health risk assessment, vitals, BMI, blood pressure, cholesterol screening, cancer screenings, immunizations review.

sections.title: Cancer Screenings
sections.content: Mammogram: $0 copay annually starting age 40. Colonoscopy: $0 copay every 10 years starting age 45. Cervical cancer screening (Pap + HPV): $0 copay every 3-5 years starting age 21. Lung CT scan: $0 copay annually for high-risk smokers age 50-80.

sections.title: Immunizations
sections.content: All ACIP-recommended vaccines are covered at $0 cost-sharing at in-network pharmacies and physician offices. Includes flu, COVID-19, pneumonia, shingles, HPV, Tdap, and RSV vaccines.

sections.title: Coverage
sections.content: Well-child visits per AAP Bright Futures schedule: $0 copay for all recommended visits from birth through age 21. Coverage includes 14 visits from birth to age 3, then annually from age 4-21.

sections.title: Screenings
sections.content: Vision, hearing, developmental, autism (M-CHAT at 18/24 months), lead, anemia, and lipid screenings covered at $0 when part of well-child visit. Separate office visit for treatment of identified conditions billed at regular copay.

sections.title: Oral Health
sections.content: Fluoride varnish application: $0 copay at primary care visit for children 6 months to 5 years. Dental referral at 12 months. Separate dental benefit applies for dental cleanings and treatment.

sections.title: Diabetes Prevention Program
sections.content: CDC-recognized Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) covered at $0 for members with prediabetes (A1C 5.7-6.4% or fasting glucose 100-125 mg/dL). Program provides 16 core sessions over 6 months plus 6 post-core sessions.

sections.title: Weight Management
sections.content: Intensive behavioral counseling for obesity: $0 copay, up to 26 sessions per year for members with BMI >= 30. Telehealth weight management programs covered equivalent to in-person.

sections.title: Smoking Cessation
sections.content: Tobacco cessation counseling: $0 copay, up to 8 sessions per year. FDA-approved cessation medications (nicotine patches, gum, bupropion, varenicline) covered at $0 with prescription, regardless of formulary tier.

sections.title: Referral Requirements
sections.content: HMO plan members require a referral from their primary care physician (PCP) to see an in-network specialist. PPO plan members do not require a referral for in-network specialists. Out-of-network specialist visits require referral and preauthorization for all plan types.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: In-network specialist visit: $50 copay. Out-of-network specialist: 40% coinsurance after deductible. Specialist visits for ongoing chronic conditions: $50 copay per visit, preauthorization required after 12 visits per year.

sections.title: Standing Referrals
sections.content: Members with chronic conditions requiring ongoing specialist care may request a standing referral valid for 12 months and up to 12 visits. Standing referral requests submitted by PCP with documentation of ongoing need.

sections.title: Direct Access Specialties
sections.content: Members may self-refer (no PCP referral needed) to OB/GYN, dermatology, mental health providers, and optometrists for routine care. Emergency specialist care does not require referral.

sections.title: When Authorized
sections.content: Out-of-network referral authorized when: (1) no in-network provider with appropriate specialty within 30 miles, (2) in-network provider has wait time exceeding 30 days for urgent condition, (3) continuity of care with existing provider during transition period.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Authorized out-of-network referral: billed at in-network rates. Member pays in-network specialist copay of $50. Unauthorized out-of-network care: 40% coinsurance after separate out-of-network deductible of $3,000.

sections.title: Continuity of Care
sections.content: New enrollees may continue care with out-of-network providers for up to 90 days at in-network rates during care transition. Members with ongoing treatment for serious conditions: 12-month continuity of care period.

sections.title: Coverage
sections.content: Laboratory tests ordered by an in-network provider are covered when medically necessary. Routine lab tests (CBC, CMP, lipid panel, thyroid) covered at $0 copay when part of annual wellness visit. Diagnostic lab tests: $25 copay.

sections.title: Facility Requirements
sections.content: Lab tests must be performed at in-network laboratories (Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, and contracted hospital labs). Out-of-network lab testing is covered only when no in-network lab is available within 15 miles.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Genetic testing requires preauthorization. Advanced imaging labs (MRI, CT, PET) require preauthorization. Routine diagnostic labs and standard imaging (X-ray, ultrasound) do not require preauthorization.

sections.title: Frequency Limits
sections.content: Repeat testing within 90 days for same diagnosis requires clinical justification. Annual preventive screenings covered per USPSTF guidelines without frequency limits.

sections.title: Coverage
sections.content: MRI, CT, and PET scans are covered when medically necessary and ordered by an in-network provider. Non-contrast CT: $100 copay. Contrast CT: $150 copay. MRI: $150 copay. PET scan: $200 copay.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: All MRI, CT, and PET scans require preauthorization regardless of indication. Preauthorization must be obtained before scheduling. Emergency imaging does not require prior authorization; plan must be notified within 24 hours.

sections.title: Preferred Facilities
sections.content: Advanced imaging at preferred radiology centers billed at lower cost. Hospital-based imaging copay is $50 higher than freestanding imaging center copay. Teleradiology for reads is covered when ordered by treating physician.

sections.title: Coverage
sections.content: Genetic testing is covered for hereditary cancer syndromes (BRCA1/2, Lynch syndrome), pharmacogenomics relevant to prescribed medications, prenatal screening, and rare disease diagnosis when clinically indicated.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: All genetic and genomic testing requires preauthorization. Request must include clinical indication, family history, prior test results, and ordering physician attestation that results will change clinical management.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Approved genetic testing: $100 copay per test panel. Direct-to-consumer genetic testing is not covered. Genetic counseling: $50 specialist copay; covered pre- and post-testing.

sections.title: Exclusions
sections.content: Whole genome sequencing for wellness purposes, ancestry testing, and predictive testing without confirmed family history or clinical indication are not covered.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Physical therapy is covered when prescribed by a physician and medically necessary for treatment of injury, illness, or post-surgical rehabilitation. Must be performed by a licensed physical therapist.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Physical therapy: $30 copay per visit. Occupational therapy: $30 copay per visit. Speech therapy: $30 copay per visit. Deductible does not apply to therapy copays.

sections.title: Visit Limits and Authorization
sections.content: First 12 visits per calendar year covered without preauthorization. Visits 13-30 require preauthorization with documented functional progress. More than 30 visits require specialist-level review and evidence of continued functional gains.

sections.title: Telehealth PT
sections.content: Telehealth physical therapy covered at $30 copay for appropriate conditions. In-person required for: initial evaluation, manual therapy techniques, and modalities requiring direct contact.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Cardiac rehabilitation is covered for members who have experienced heart attack (MI), coronary artery bypass surgery, stable angina, heart valve repair/replacement, or heart failure (EF < 35%).

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Phase II cardiac rehab: $30 copay per session. Maximum 36 sessions covered per cardiac event. Additional sessions up to 72 total available with documentation of continued medical necessity.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Cardiac rehabilitation requires referral from cardiologist or cardiac surgeon with qualifying diagnosis. Preauthorization approved for initial 36 sessions. Additional sessions require documentation of compliance and functional progress.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Chiropractic care is covered for musculoskeletal conditions when medically necessary. Must be provided by a licensed chiropractor (DC) at an in-network facility.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Chiropractic visit: $30 copay per visit. Annual limit of 20 visits covered. Additional visits beyond 20 require preauthorization and are covered at 50% after deductible.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: First 20 visits per year do not require preauthorization. Visits beyond 20 require documented evidence of functional improvement and that further treatment is medically necessary.

sections.title: Exclusions
sections.content: Chiropractic care for maintenance or wellness (not medically necessary acute/subacute conditions) is not covered. Nutritional supplements, homeopathic treatments, and non-musculoskeletal conditions are not covered.

sections.title: Coverage
sections.content: PPO members may receive care from out-of-network providers at reduced benefit levels. Out-of-network care is covered after separate out-of-network deductible is met. Plan pays 60% of allowed amount for out-of-network services.

sections.title: Out-of-Network Deductible
sections.content: Out-of-network deductible: $3,000 individual / $6,000 family per calendar year. Out-of-network out-of-pocket maximum: $9,000 individual / $18,000 family. In-network payments do not count toward out-of-network deductible.

sections.title: Allowed Amount
sections.content: Plan pays based on Medicare-based allowed amount or 110% of Medicare rate for out-of-network services. Member is responsible for difference between billed charge and allowed amount (balance billing) for non-emergency services.

sections.title: No Surprises Act Protections
sections.content: Surprise billing protections apply to emergency services and certain non-emergency services at in-network facilities. Air ambulance out-of-network billing protections apply per federal law.

sections.title: Emergency Services
sections.content: Emergency services from out-of-network providers covered at in-network cost-sharing rates. Members may not be balance billed for emergency care. Applies to emergency facilities and emergency medicine physicians, anesthesiologists, and radiologists.

sections.title: Non-Emergency Surprise Billing
sections.content: Members receiving non-emergency care at in-network facilities may not be balance billed by out-of-network providers who were not chosen by the member (e.g., anesthesiologists, assistants). Good Faith Estimate required for scheduled services.

sections.title: Independent Dispute Resolution
sections.content: When plan and out-of-network provider disagree on payment, either party may initiate Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process. IDR decision binding on both parties. Member cost-sharing not affected by IDR outcome.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Emergency care received out-of-network is subject to in-network cost-sharing only. Member pays in-network emergency room copay of $350 plus applicable deductible. No additional out-of-network cost-sharing applies.

sections.title: Post-Stabilization
sections.content: Once stabilized, plan may arrange transfer to in-network facility. If member declines transfer, out-of-network rates apply to post-stabilization care. Plan must notify member of available in-network alternatives.

sections.title: Conflicting Policy Note
sections.content: This policy supersedes POL-OON-001 for emergency situations. Out-of-network emergency deductible does NOT apply per No Surprises Act. Only in-network deductible and cost-sharing apply to emergency out-of-network care.

sections.title: Inpatient Rates
sections.content: Inpatient acute care reimbursement based on MS-DRG methodology at 145% of Medicare base rate. High-cost outlier payments triggered when costs exceed DRG rate by 150%. Carve-out rates apply for: transplant services, burn care, NICU (Level III/IV).

sections.title: Outpatient Rates
sections.content: Outpatient services reimbursed at 130% of Medicare APC rates. Bundled payment applies to: joint replacement (30-day episode), cardiac catheterization, colonoscopy. Professional fees billed separately at RVU-based rates.

sections.title: Quality Incentives
sections.content: Value-based performance bonus: up to 5% of annual contract value based on HEDIS measures, readmission rates, patient satisfaction (HCAHPS), and appropriate utilization metrics. Bonus calculated quarterly.

sections.title: Claims Submission
sections.content: Clean claims must be submitted within 180 days of date of service. Plan must pay clean claims within 30 days (electronic) or 45 days (paper). Interest of 1.5% per month applies to late payments.

sections.title: Primary Care Rates
sections.content: Primary care evaluation and management (E&M) services reimbursed at 110% of Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS). Chronic care management (CCM): $62 per month for qualifying patients. Annual wellness visit: $175 per visit.

sections.title: Specialist Rates
sections.content: Specialist E&M services: 115% of MPFS. Surgical procedures: 120% of MPFS global rate. Anesthesia: 100% of Medicare base units at $23 per unit. Pathology and radiology reads: 105% of MPFS.

sections.title: Telehealth Rates
sections.content: Telehealth services reimbursed at 100% of in-person rate for audio-video visits. Audio-only telehealth: 85% of in-person rate. Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM): $50 setup fee plus $20 per month per enrolled patient.

sections.title: Value-Based Arrangements
sections.content: Primary care providers participating in shared savings program receive per-member-per-month (PMPM) care management payment of $8. Shared savings distributed annually based on total cost of care and quality metrics.

sections.title: Clean Claim Definition
sections.content: A clean claim includes: valid member ID, valid provider NPI, date of service, place of service code, diagnosis codes (ICD-10-CM), procedure codes (CPT/HCPCS), billed amount, and signature on file attestation.

sections.title: Denial Reasons
sections.content: Common denial reasons: (1) Lack of preauthorization, (2) Non-covered service, (3) Coordination of benefits (COB) issue, (4) Duplicate claim, (5) Timely filing exceeded, (6) Member not eligible on date of service, (7) Medical necessity not established.

sections.title: Appeal Rights
sections.content: Providers may appeal claim denials within 180 days. First-level appeal: 30 days for decision. Second-level appeal to independent reviewer: 45 days. Expedited appeal for urgent care: 72 hours.

sections.title: Recoupment
sections.content: Plan may recoup overpayments identified within 24 months of original payment. Recoupment notice provided 30 days in advance. Provider may contest recoupment through the appeals process.

sections.title: Primary vs Secondary
sections.content: COB order determined by: (1) Subscriber's own plan is primary for subscriber, (2) Birthday rule for dependents when both parents have coverage, (3) Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP) rules apply when Medicare is involved.

sections.title: Secondary Payment
sections.content: As secondary payer, plan pays the lesser of: (a) what it would pay if primary, or (b) the balance remaining after primary payment. Member cannot receive more than 100% of claim through combined benefits.

sections.title: Medicare as Secondary Payer
sections.content: When member has group coverage as active employee and Medicare, group plan is primary. Employer groups of 20+ must offer active employees the same coverage as non-Medicare members. MSP violation penalties apply.

sections.title: Coverage
sections.content: Durable medical equipment (DME) is covered when medically necessary and ordered by a treating physician. DME must be used primarily for medical purposes, able to withstand repeated use, and appropriate for home use.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: DME: 20% coinsurance after deductible. Rental vs purchase: Plan authorizes rental for equipment expected to be needed less than 13 months. For equipment needed longer, plan covers purchase. Capped rental at 13 months equals purchase.

sections.title: Covered Equipment
sections.content: Covered DME includes: wheelchairs (manual/power), hospital beds, oxygen equipment, CPAP/BiPAP for documented sleep apnea, insulin pumps, blood pressure monitors, and hearing aids ($1,500 per ear every 3 years).

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Power wheelchairs, hospital beds, oxygen equipment, CPAP/BiPAP, and prosthetics require preauthorization. Manual wheelchairs and standard DME under $500 do not require preauthorization.

sections.title: Prenatal Care
sections.content: Prenatal visits covered at $0 copay as preventive care for first prenatal appointment and routine prenatal visits. OB/GYN prenatal care: no referral required. Certified nurse midwife (CNM) prenatal care covered equivalent to OB.

sections.title: Labor and Delivery
sections.content: Vaginal delivery: $500 inpatient copay. C-section: $500 inpatient copay (same as vaginal). Minimum hospital stay: 48 hours for vaginal delivery, 96 hours for C-section, per federal law. Early discharge covered if physician-approved.

sections.title: Newborn Coverage
sections.content: Newborn covered under mother's policy for first 30 days. After 30 days, newborn must be enrolled as a dependent. Newborn screenings and hearing tests: $0 copay as preventive care. NICU coverage: $500 per admission copay.

sections.title: Postpartum Care
sections.content: Postpartum visit: $0 copay within 12 weeks of delivery. Postpartum depression screening: $0 copay. Lactation counseling and breast pump: covered at $0 per ACA preventive care requirement.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.content: Home health care is covered for members who are homebound and require skilled nursing care, physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, or home health aide services on an intermittent basis.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Home health visits: $0 copay per visit when preauthorized. Home health aide: covered up to 8 hours per day, 5 days per week when skilled care is also being provided. Private duty nursing: requires separate authorization, $100/day copay.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: Home health care requires preauthorization. Initial authorization: 60 days. Continued care requires updated physician orders and documentation of ongoing medical necessity. Authorization renewed in 60-day increments.

sections.title: Exclusions
sections.content: Custodial care (assistance with activities of daily living without skilled need) is not covered under home health benefit. 24-hour private duty nursing for convenience is not covered.

sections.title: Covered Services
sections.content: Telehealth covers: primary care visits, mental health therapy, specialist consultations, dermatology (store-and-forward), chronic disease management, post-surgical follow-up, and urgent care for non-emergency conditions.

sections.title: Cost Sharing
sections.content: Telehealth primary care: $25 copay (same as in-person). Telehealth urgent care: $75 copay (same as in-person urgent care). Telehealth specialist: $50 copay (same as in-person specialist). No facility fee for telehealth.

sections.title: Technology Requirements
sections.content: Audio-video visits preferred. Audio-only visits covered when member lacks technology access or for conditions appropriate to audio-only assessment. Provider must be licensed in member's state. Out-of-state telehealth covered per interstate licensing compact.

sections.title: Preauthorization
sections.content: No preauthorization required for telehealth primary care or urgent care. Telehealth specialist visits follow same preauthorization rules as in-person specialist visits.
